jobs.title: VP, Enterprise Development & Real Estate Services - Canadian Tire Corporation
jobs.description:
Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most trusted companies and one of the country’s most recognized retail brands. Across Canadian Tire Retail, Mark’s, SportChek, Triangle Rewards and Canadian Tire Bank, we are investing in technology, data and talent to create better experiences for Canadians. This is an exciting time to join CTC and help shape how data and AI drive our next chapter of growth.

Canadian Tire Corporation is seeking a Vice President, Enterprise Development & Real Estate Services to lead the development and strategic management of one of Canada’s largest retail real estate portfolios.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Real Estate, this role will have enterprise accountability for Real Estate Development and Real Estate Services, spanning store and corporate development, portfolio and network strategy, major real estate transactions, property management, lease administration, environmental services, and more.

Job Description

This leader will operate across a highly complex stakeholder environment, partnering with senior business leaders, across key internal banners/functions as well as landlords, developers, dealers, municipalities and other external partners. The Vice President will play a critical role in shaping the future of CTC’s physical network, translating business and banner strategies into a long-term real estate plan and a prioritized, executable investment pipeline. The role requires strong strategic and commercial judgment, combined with disciplined operational leadership, to identify and advance opportunities, make sound investment decisions, navigate complex transactions and ensure CTC’s real estate portfolio and day-to-day services are effectively managed to meet the evolving needs of the business.

What You Will Do

Lead the development and execution of CTC’s enterprise real estate strategy, translating business and banner priorities into long-term plans for the store network, corporate offices and campuses, distribution and logistics facilities, and other strategic real estate investments.
Lead store development across Canada, including new stores, relocations, expansions, renewals, redevelopments, acquisitions, dispositions and other strategic real estate transactions.
Drive ongoing portfolio optimization and value creation, identifying opportunities to reposition, redevelop, intensify, acquire or dispose of assets to improve portfolio performance and support enterprise priorities.
Provide strategic leadership for CTC’s corporate real estate portfolio, including long-term planning for office and campus requirements, distribution and logistics real estate, and other enterprise properties, ensuring real estate solutions support evolving business, workforce and operational needs.
Build and manage a prioritized multi-year development pipeline across retail and corporate real estate, ensuring investments are supported by a strong strategic rationale, sound economics and a clear path to execution.
Lead site selection, market and feasibility analysis, due diligence, entitlements and the negotiation of complex leases, development agreements, acquisitions, dispositions and other significant property transactions.
Strengthen real estate investment governance and capital discipline, working closely with Finance and business leaders to improve opportunity evaluation, financial analysis, prioritization and investment decisions.
Build and maintain internal senior relationships with banner presidents and key functional leaders, as well as external relationship across landlords, developers, dealers, municipalities and other key partners, across various Real Estate matters.
Lead the Real Estate Services portfolio, including lease administration, property and lease management, occupancy costs, property tax, and more. Includes both effective day to day operations as well and build out of longer-term advancement strategy to optimize effectiveness.
As a part of Real Estate Services, lead Environmental Services, ensuring environmental risks are appropriately identified, managed and addressed across acquisitions, development, operations and the existing portfolio.
Partner closely with the Vice President, Enterprise Construction & Workplace and other enterprise functions to ensure strong connectivity from portfolio strategy and development through design, construction, occupancy and ongoing operation.
Manage key strategic real estate partnerships, including the relationship with CT REIT, to advance portfolio priorities and optimize value creation
Lead, develop and strengthen a high-performing team of real estate professionals, building enterprise capability, clear accountability, strong succession and a high performing and united team culture.

What You Will Bring

We are looking for a high-performing enterprise leader who is:

A seasoned real estate executive with broad experience across retail and corporate development, transactions, portfolio strategy and real estate operations.
A strategic and commercial thinker who can translate business priorities into clear real estate strategies, investment decisions and executable plans.
Financially astute, with the ability to assess complex investments, understand portfolio economics and make sound capital allocation recommendations and trade-offs.
An accomplished negotiator and relationship builder, comfortable managing significant transactions and diverse senior internal and external stakeholders.
A strong people leader with a track record of building high-performing teams, developing talent and creating accountability.
A pragmatic problem solver who can navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities and drive outcomes in a complex enterprise environment.
A credible senior partner who can communicate clearly, challenge constructively and influence decisions across all levels of the organization.

You Should Have

Bachelor’s degree in Real Estate, Business Administration, Finance or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in real estate development, portfolio strategy, asset/property management or a comparable multi-site environment.
Significant experience leading complex real estate development and transactions, including leases, acquisitions, dispositions and redevelopment projects.
Experience developing and executing corporate real estate, office, campus, distribution/logistics or other large-scale portfolio strategies would be a strong asset.
Strong financial acumen with demonstrated experience in investment analysis, project economics, budgeting and capital allocation.
Proven success leading large multidisciplinary teams and influencing senior stakeholders across a complex organization.
Retail, Corporate real estate, REIT or large multi-site operating experience is strongly preferred.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

jobs.description:
Our employees are at the heart of everything we do. Together, we help people, businesses, and society prosper in good times and be resilient in bad times.

Our employee promise represents Intact’s commitment to you in exchange for living our Values, striving to do your best work, being open to change and investing in your career. In return, we promise to provide support, opportunities and performance-led financial rewards at a workplace where you can shape the future, win as a team and grow with us.

Pay at Intact is about much more than just salary.

Flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work model
Possibility to purchase up to 5 extra days off per year
Multiple benefits offered to support physical and mental wellbeing, including telemedicine, Wellness account and much more
Share plan & other savings: up to 12% of salary or even more (ask how you could earn guaranteed income for life)

Salary Range (but Not Limited To)

149,600 - 182,800

Annual Bonus Target, Based On The Base Salary, With a Potential Payout Of Up To Double The Target (subject To Personal And Company Performance)

20%

As part of our commitment to Win As A Team
, we share our success with employees through our annual bonus plan and Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) – with Intact matching 50% of your net shares.

Our pension offerings provide flexibility and long-term security for our employees beyond their careers. We are one of the few companies offering the opportunity to receive guaranteed income for life via our defined benefit pension plan.

Salary for the candidate will be determined taking into consideration a number of factors including: experience, skills, qualifications, anticipated contribution to role, internal equity, etc. The salary range presented above is based on a 35-hour workweek and would represent a majority of different candidate profiles. However, we encourage candidates who may fall outside of this range to apply as well.

About The Role

We are creating a new leadership role to shape and advance our Technology Financial Controls capability across Canada and the United States.

As our organization continues to evolve, this leader will establish the strategy, governance and operating model required to support a strong and scalable technology control environment, including the continued development of our SOX 404 framework across technology.

Working at the intersection of Technology, Finance, Risk, Internal Audit and business transformation, you will provide strategic leadership on technology risks that can impact financial reporting. You will partner closely with our Elevate and Advisory teams and with senior technology and business leaders to embed effective controls into how technology is designed, developed, changed and operated.

This is not simply a role focused on testing compliance. You will have the mandate to build and mature the capability, strengthen accountability, influence major technology transformations and modernize how financial controls are designed, monitored and sustained.

Success will require deep SOX and technology-controls expertise, strong understanding of modern software development environments, and the ability to lead significant organizational and behavioural change.

What You'll Do Here

Set the strategy and strengthen the control environment

Define and lead the IT Financial Controls strategy and roadmap across Canada and the U.S., aligning financial reporting, technology and transformation priorities.
Establish the operating model, governance and accountabilities across Technology, Finance, Risk, business control owners and assurance partners.
Provide leadership for the technology components of the SOX program, including ITGCs, ITACs, Segregation of Duties and other technology-enabled financial controls.
Oversee control design and assessment, testing quality, deficiency management and sustainable remediation, ensuring significant and systemic risks are appropriately challenged and escalated.

Embed controls and drive transformation

Partner with technology and software engineering leaders to embed SOX and financial-control requirements into technology development, change, access and release processes.
Ensure major technology transformations, system implementations and software changes appropriately address financial-reporting risks and control requirements.
Modernize the control environment through automation, continuous monitoring, data-driven risk management and improved reporting, partnering closely with Elevate, Advisory and transformation teams.
Challenge legacy practices and drive controls that are effective, scalable and proportionate to risk.

Advise, influence and lead assurance partnerships

Act as a trusted advisor to senior Technology, Finance, Risk and business leaders on control risks, remediation strategies, transformation impacts and investment decisions.
Provide executive-level visibility into significant deficiencies, systemic risk themes and remediation progress.
Lead the approach to Internal and External Audit relationships, strengthening coordination while maintaining clear accountability between control ownership, advisory and independent assurance.

Build and lead the capability

Lead a team while building capabilities across SOX, financial controls, technology risk, software engineering and transformation.
Own workforce planning, talent development, succession and resource allocation across the function.
Establish clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and strong business partnership.

What You Bring To The Table

10+ years of progressive experience in IT financial controls, SOX, technology risk, audit or a related discipline, with demonstrated leadership experience.
Deep knowledge of SOX 404, ITGCs, ITACs, Segregation of Duties and financial-reporting controls, ideally within a U.S. public-company environment.
Strong understanding of technology and modern software-development environments, with the ability to embed practical controls into development, change, access and release processes.
A track record of building or transforming control programs and leading complex change across Technology, Finance, Risk and business teams.
Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders, navigate complex risk decisions and translate technical control issues into clear business priorities and actions.
CPA, CISA, CIA or similar designation is an asset, as is experience in financial services, insurance, Big Four or another complex regulated environment.
For candidates located in Quebec, bilingualism is required considering the necessity to interact on a regular basis with English-speaking colleagues across the country.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Data and AI
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Senior Director, Data & AI will lead VetStrategy’s enterprise Data, Analytics and AI agenda, building the capabilities required to turn data into better decisions, better client and patient experiences, more productive clinics, and stronger business performance.

This role will be responsible for defining and executing the Data & AI strategy across the organization, establishing a trusted enterprise data foundation, modernizing analytics and reporting, and identifying and scaling practical AI solutions that create measurable value.

The successful candidate will combine strong technical and data leadership with commercial judgment and an ability to work closely with Operations, Finance, Marketing, HR, Technology and our clinic teams.

This is not primarily a reporting or technology role. It is a business transformation role using data and AI to help VetStrategy operate more effectively, understand its customers and clinics more deeply, and make faster, better decisions.

Key Accountabilities

Data & AI Strategy

Define and execute the enterprise Data & AI strategy aligned to VetStrategy's business priorities.
Develop a clear roadmap across data platforms, analytics, business intelligence, advanced analytics, AI and data governance.
Establish a disciplined approach to prioritizing Data & AI investments based on business value, feasibility and speed to impact.
Stay current on developments in AI and emerging technologies and translate them into practical opportunities for VetStrategy.

Enterprise Data Foundation

Lead the development of a trusted, scalable enterprise data platform integrating data across clinical, customer, operational, financial and workforce systems.
Improve the availability, consistency, quality and accessibility of enterprise data.
Establish common definitions and enterprise metrics so leaders and clinics operate from a consistent version of performance.
Partner with Technology teams on data architecture, integration, security and platform decisions.
Reduce manual data extraction and spreadsheet dependency through automation and self-service capabilities.

Analytics & Business Intelligence

Build an analytics capability that moves the organization from reporting what happened to understanding why it happened and predicting what will happen accompanied with what actions should be taken.
Develop executive, regional, district and clinic-level performance insights that enable leaders to identify opportunities and intervene quickly.
Build predictive and diagnostic analytical capabilities including forecasting, segmentation, propensity modelling and performance-driver analysis.
Create self-service tools that allow leaders to access insights without requiring constant analyst support.

Artificial Intelligence

Establish and lead VetStrategy's enterprise AI roadmap.
Identify and deploy AI opportunities that improve both clinic and corporate workflows.
Build practical use cases for generative AI, machine learning, intelligent automation and decision support.
Partner with business leaders to redesign processes rather than simply layering AI onto existing workflows.
Establish frameworks for responsible AI adoption, including data privacy, security, governance, model risk and human oversight.
Measure AI initiatives based on realized business outcomes, productivity gains and adoption—not simply technology deployment.

Data Governance & Quality

Establish enterprise data governance including ownership, definitions, quality standards and accountability.
Improve data quality at source and address systemic issues affecting reporting and operational decision-making.
Create clear ownership of critical data domains and KPIs.
Partner with Technology, Finance, Operations and other functions to strengthen data controls and integrity.
Ensure appropriate compliance with privacy, security and regulatory requirements.

Business Partnership & Value Creation

Work directly with senior executives and functional leaders to translate business questions into analytical solutions.
Become a trusted thought partner to Operations and clinic leadership, helping teams understand the drivers behind performance.
Establish clear value cases for major Data & AI initiatives and track benefits after implementation.
Bring together data from multiple sources to identify opportunities that may not be visible within individual functions.
Promote greater use of experimentation, analytics and evidence-based decision-making across the organization.

Leadership & Capability Building

Build and lead a high-performing Data & AI organization spanning data engineering, analytics, BI, data science and AI capabilities.
Define the appropriate combination of internal capability, external partners and technology platforms.
Develop strong talent and succession pipelines across the function.
Establish modern ways of working with clear product ownership, prioritization and accountability for outcomes.
Create a culture focused on curiosity, simplicity, pace, quality and business impact.
Increase data literacy across VetStrategy so leaders can confidently interpret and act on data.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will be demonstrated through outcomes including:

Increased trust in enterprise data and reporting.
Faster access to actionable performance insights.
Reduced manual reporting and spreadsheet dependency.
Greater adoption of self-service analytics.
Improved ability to identify the drivers of clinic performance.
Measurable revenue, productivity, cost and customer improvements enabled through analytics.
Successful deployment and adoption of high-value AI use cases.
Improved enterprise data quality and governance.
Clear return on investment from Data & AI initiatives.
Stronger data literacy and evidence-based decision-making throughout the organization.

Experience & Qualifications

The successful candidate will ideally bring:

10+ years of progressive experience across data, analytics, AI, digital or technology, including significant leadership responsibility.
Experience leading enterprise Data & Analytics transformation in a complex, multi-location or distributed operating environment.
Demonstrated ability to connect data and technology investment directly to commercial and operational outcomes.
Strong understanding of modern data platforms, analytics architecture, BI, data science, machine learning and generative AI.
Experience establishing enterprise data governance and improving data quality.
Experience building and leading multidisciplinary data teams.
Demonstrated experience working with senior executives and influencing across organizational boundaries.
Ability to simplify complex analytical or technical concepts for non-technical audiences.
Strong change leadership skills and experience driving adoption of new capabilities across an organization.
Experience in healthcare, veterinary services, retail, consumer services or another multi-site operating environment would be an asset.

Leadership Attributes

The Senior Director, Data & AI Will Be

Business-led: starts with the business problem rather than the technology.
Commercially minded: understands how data translates into revenue, productivity, customer outcomes and enterprise value.
Curious: constantly asks why performance differs and what the data can tell us.
Pragmatic: balances long-term architecture with the need to deliver value quickly.
Outcome-oriented: measures success through adoption and business impact rather than delivery of technology alone.
Collaborative: works across functions and recognizes that Data & AI transformation requires shared ownership.
A simplifier: turns complexity into clear insights, priorities and actions.
A builder: capable of creating the team, platforms, operating model and culture required for a modern Data & AI function.

We dare to innovate, encourage entrepreneurial thinking and identify opportunities to succeed in a changing world.

About Dalhousie University

Dalhousie University is Atlantic Canada’s leading research-intensive university and a driver of the region’s intellectual, social and economic development. Located in the heart of Halifax, Nova Scotia, with an Agricultural Campus in Truro/Bible Hill, Dalhousie is a truly national and international university, with more than half of our almost 21,000 students coming from outside of the province. Our 6,000 faculty and staff foster a vibrant, purpose-driven community, that celebrated 200 years of academic excellence in 2018.

Job Summary

Dalhousie University is embarking on a significant transformation of its administrative services, reshaping how services are organized, delivered and enabled by technology across the institution. The multi-year Service Modernization Program will simplify and standardize processes, modernize service delivery, introduce new operating models and enterprise technologies, and strengthen the University’s ability to deliver high-quality, sustainable services for students, faculty and staff. Reporting to the Chief Enterprise Transformation Officer, the Director, Change Management will play a pivotal leadership role in this transformation, building organizational readiness, engaging the university community and enabling the adoption of new processes, technologies, roles and ways of working.

Key Responsibilities

Shape and lead the enterprise change and adoption strategy for Dalhousie’s multi-year Service Modernization Program, building the organizational readiness, leadership alignment and commitment required to transform how administrative services are delivered.
Serve as a trusted strategic advisor and thought partner to senior leaders, using change insights, stakeholder perspectives and organizational readiness data to anticipate risks, navigate complex transformation decisions and accelerate adoption.
Build and mobilize a university-wide change network, engaging leaders, faculty, staff and other stakeholders as active partners in the transformation and creating meaningful opportunities to shape, champion and sustain new ways of working.
Lead enterprise change impact assessments, working collaboratively with People & Culture, functional and program teams to develop workforce transition strategies and prepare the organization for new operating models, service delivery approaches, processes, technologies, roles and accountabilities.
Set the strategy for communications, learning and capability development, creating targeted experiences that help leaders and employees understand the transformation, build confidence and develop the capabilities required to succeed in the future operating model.
Define and measure what successful adoption looks like, using readiness, adoption, experience and benefits measures to identify where intervention is needed, strengthen outcomes and embed a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, service excellence and accountability.

Note

The successful applicant will be eligible for hybrid work (combination of in-person work on campus and remote work from within Nova Scotia) as agreed by all parties based on operational requirements and university guidelines.

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in Business, Human Resources, Organizational Development, Public Administration, Education, or a related discipline, plus eight to ten years of progressive experience leading large-scale organizational change and transformation initiatives, including experience supervising and leading teams, (or an equivalent combination of training and experience).
Change Management Certification or equivalent, with demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning), digital transformation, operating model, or business transformation programs.
Extensive experience developing and executing enterprise change management strategies, organizational readiness plans, stakeholder engagement initiatives, and change adoption frameworks within complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
Experience supporting organizational design, workforce transition planning, operating model implementation, and the adoption of new business processes, technologies, and ways of working.
Exceptional facilitation, negotiation, relationship management, and executive communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across academic, administrative, and governance environments.
Experience establishing enterprise change networks and developing change adoption, organizational readiness, and benefits realization measurement frameworks.

Assets

Experience leading change management within higher education, public sector, or similarly complex organizations.
Experience supporting large-scale ERP implementations and enterprise service management transformations.
Knowledge of organizational development, continuous improvement, workforce planning, and service modernization principles and practices.

jobs.title: Vice President of Interconnects Product Line Management
jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

How You Will Contribute

We are seeking an entrepreneurial and commercially driven Vice President of Interconnects Product Line Management (PLM)
to lead global product strategy, roadmap execution, and P&L performance for our Interconnects portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Product officer, this individual plays a pivotal role in scaling the interconnects portfolio to triple the revenue in FY27 on the path to $1B
. You will own the end-to-end lifecycle of our high-speed optical interconnect products (400G, 800G, 1.6T, and emerging 3.2T architectures), capturing market share across hyperscale data center interconnect (DCI), AI/ML clusters, and metro/long-haul networks.

You will partner closely with R&D, supply chain, services and global sales and marketing to translate complex market inflection points into high-margin, differentiated hardware and software solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy & Vision: Define and execute the multi-year product vision, investment strategy and technology roadmap for the Interconnects business unit, establishing competitive differentiation across coherent optical transceivers (ZR/ZR+), co-packaged optics (CPO), pluggable optics, and intra-data center interconnects.
P&L Ownership & Commercial Growth: Own full P&L accountability for a three hundred-million-dollar-plus product line, driving aggressive top-line growth, gross margin expansion, and disciplined lifecycle management with a goal of tripling the revenue in FY27.
Hyperscale & Tier-1 Customer Engagement: Serve as the executive product sponsor for top-tier hyperscalers, AI infrastructure builders, and Tier-1 service providers, securing critical design wins and shaping custom ASIC/DSP and optical specifications.
Cross-Functional Execution: Lead and scale a global organization of Product Line Managers, working seamlessly with R&D, Operations, Sales and Global Supply Chain to ensure on-time NPI (New Product Introduction) delivery and high-volume manufacturing ramps.
Ecosystem & Standards Leadership: Represent the company across key industry standards bodies and MSAs (e.g., OIF, IEEE, Ethernet Alliance), influencing next-generation optical form factors and interoperability standards.
Strategic Partnerships & M&A: Identify strategic technology partnerships, ecosystem alliances, and supply chain vertical integration opportunities to accelerate time-to-market and strengthen competitive moats

What Makes You an Exceptional Candidate?

The successful candidate is a results-oriented, strategic and inspirational leader who knows how to drive performance, has a passion for the business, and a fierce competitive drive.

Executive Leadership: 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in optical networking, semiconductors, or high-speed data center infrastructure, with at least 5+ years at the VP/SVP level managing a $300M+ P&L and scaling high-growth product lines.
Deep Domain Expertise: Proven track record in optical interconnects, coherent DSPs, silicon photonics, high-speed transceivers (400G/800G/1.6T), and hyperscale AI/data center architectures.
Commercial Acumen: Demonstrated success winning Tier-1 and hyperscale qualifications, navigating complex BOM cost-down curves, and scaling high-volume manufacturing ramps.
Strategic & Technical Fluency: Ability to bridge deep technical architecture discussions with C-level commercial strategy; bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Physics, or Optical Sciences required (Master’s or MBA preferred).
Agile Team Builder: Proven capability to attract, mentor, and scale high-performing, globally distributed PLM teams in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Performance Measures

Revenue Targets: Achieving quarterly and annual revenue targets to keep the business unit on its trajectory toward tripling the revenue in FY27.
Gross Margin Expansion: Driving product gross margins upward through pricing discipline, higher-value product mix (e.g., shifting toward 800G/1.6T coherent pluggables), and BOM (Bill of Materials) cost-down initiatives.
Hyperscale & Tier-1 Design Wins: Securing architectural design-ins and qualification milestones at top-tier cloud, AI cluster, and telecom customers.
Customer Concentration & Diversification: Expanding wallet share within anchor hyperscale accounts while onboarding new Tier-1/Tier-2 customers to ensure customer diversification.
Market Share Gains: Tracking revenue share growth against key optical interconnect competitors across target segments (e.g., DCI, intra-data center, metro coherent).

As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

How You Will Contribute

We are seeking an entrepreneurial and commercially driven Vice President of Interconnects Product Line Management (PLM)
to lead global product strategy, roadmap execution, and P&L performance for our Interconnects portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Product officer, this individual plays a pivotal role in scaling the interconnects portfolio to triple the revenue in FY27 on the path to $1B
. You will own the end-to-end lifecycle of our high-speed optical interconnect products (400G, 800G, 1.6T, and emerging 3.2T architectures), capturing market share across hyperscale data center interconnect (DCI), AI/ML clusters, and metro/long-haul networks.

You will partner closely with R&D, supply chain, services and global sales and marketing to translate complex market inflection points into high-margin, differentiated hardware and software solutions.

Portfolio Strategy & Vision: Define and execute the multi-year product vision, investment strategy and technology roadmap for the Interconnects business unit, establishing competitive differentiation across coherent optical transceivers (ZR/ZR+), co-packaged optics (CPO), pluggable optics, and intra-data center interconnects.
P&L Ownership & Commercial Growth: Own full P&L accountability for a three hundred-million-dollar-plus product line, driving aggressive top-line growth, gross margin expansion, and disciplined lifecycle management with a goal of tripling the revenue in FY27.

jobs.title: Director of Sales and Marketing - Hotels
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Director of Sales and Marketing - Hotels to join our team!

Are you a strategic thinker with a passion for driving sales success? Join us as our Director of Sales and Marketing - Hotels and shape the commercial success of our hotel portfolio.

Job Description

As the Director of Sales and Marketing – Hotels, you are responsible for driving revenue growth, expanding corporate accounts, and maximizing commercial performance across the organization’s proprietarily branded hotel portfolio. With a primary focus on corporate business development, this role will lead the Hotel portfolio’s sales team, while working collaboratively with General Managers Revenue Management to identify opportunities, optimize market segmentation, and ensure each property is attracting the right business at the right time to maximize revenue and profitability.

Key Focuses

Corporate Accounts & Business Development

Lead the acquisition, development, and retention of key corporate accounts to increase revenue and market share across the portfolio.
Identify new business opportunities, develop strategic partnerships, and maximize existing account potential through proactive sales efforts.
Negotiate corporate rate agreements and develop account strategies that generate measurable revenue growth.

Commercial Strategy & Market Segmentation

Collaborate with hotel leadership and Revenue Management to develop commercial strategies tailored to each property's market and business needs.
Analyze business mix, demand patterns, and market segments to identify revenue opportunities across corporate, group, and transient business.
Align sales efforts with occupancy needs, rate positioning, and profitability objectives to optimize revenue performance.

Hotel-Level Revenue Optimization

Work directly with individual hotels to identify revenue gaps and develop targeted sales initiatives by market segment, day of week, and season.
Ensure corporate and group business complements existing demand and supports the most profitable business mix.
Balance portfolio-wide business opportunities with individual hotel needs to maximize revenue and profitability.

Sales Leadership & Collaboration

Provide commercial leadership and support to General Managers and hotel sales teams in achieving revenue objectives.
Establish sales priorities, performance expectations, and accountability while fostering a proactive sales culture.
Coach and collaborate with hotel teams to strengthen business development and account management effectiveness.

Revenue Performance & Accountability

Partner with Revenue Management to establish commercial targets, forecasts, and performance measures.
Monitor account production, market segment performance, and revenue trends to identify opportunities and implement corrective strategies.
Evaluate commercial success based on revenue contribution, market share growth, and overall hotel profitability.

Experience/Passions/Education

Minimum of 5 years of experience in a senior sales role within the hospitality industry, preferably in a multi-property hotel environment.
Post-secondary education in Business, Marketing, Hospitality, or a related field preferred.
Demonstrated expertise in hotel sales, corporate account management, business development, relationship building, and contract negotiation.
Strong understanding of hotel revenue management, market segmentation, and commercial strategy.
Strong leadership, communication, analytical, and strategic planning skills, with a proven ability to drive measurable business results.
Proactive, collaborative, and results-driven, with the ability to influence, engage, and support hotel leadership teams.
Experience developing and executing sales and marketing strategies that drive revenue growth, strengthen brand positioning, and increase market share.

Pomeroy Perks

Competitive wages and Health and Wellness benefit plan.
Paid on-the-job training with additional learning opportunities.
Growth and development opportunities, both personal and professional.
Personal days: 5 per year after 90 days of continuous full-time employment.
Pomeroy Stay Travel Program.

Working Conditions

This position is based out of the Calgary corporate office and requires travel to support hotel operations and business initiatives. Occasional long days and weekends may be required to meet business demands or deadlines. This position operates in a fast-paced environment that requires a high level of strategic collaboration and engagement with internal and external stakeholders.

About Pomeroy Lodging

Pomeroy Lodging is Western Canada’s leader in hospitality and lodging. Driven to meet every need, we own and operate a comprehensive range of hotels and resorts throughout the West. Our investment goes well beyond the walls of our hotels and the land we build on. Pomeroy Lodging is committed to investing heavily in our people, properties, and communities.
